financials_interim.notes: Source: Alumex PLC Interim Financial Statements for the Three Months Ended 30 June 2026 (unaudited, signed 23 Jul 2026), downloaded from CSE cdn. This is the FIRST financial_statements row entered for ALUM in this DB, so only YoY (vs the filing's own comparative quarter ended 30 June 2025) is computed, no QoQ. Alumex has a 31 March financial year end -> this is Q1 FY2026/27. Single-entity filing (no separate Group/Company columns; Alumex PLC has no subsidiaries consolidated in this statement) -> entered as ONE row, basis=GROUP per project convention for single-entity filers. Income statement p.2, balance sheet p.3, statement of cash flows p.5, EPS/shares note p.6. Sign convention: cost_of_sales and finance_costs stored as positive magnitudes; capex stored as positive magnitude; cash_from_operations/investing/financing keep natural (negative-for-outflow) sign. tax_expense: the filing's own line is 'Tax Reversal/(Expense)' = a credit of 18,184 this quarter (vs an expense of 9,075 a year earlier) -> stored as -18,184 (negative = credit) so that profit_before_tax(131,754) - tax_expense(-18,184) = profit_after_tax(149,938) exactly. operating_profit = 'Results from operating activities' (270,219 vs 218,856). finance_income (185,887) and finance_costs (324,352) are both disclosed gross on the income statement (unlike ACL/APLA's single net line) -- both stored as printed. depreciation_amortization (130,101) taken from the cash flow statement addback (p.5); the filing gives no separate PPE-only D&A note. short_term_borrowings = 'Short-term interest bearing borrowings' (7,740,597) + 'Current portion of long term interest bearing borrowings' (627,012) = 8,367,609, matching this project's ACL-precedent of combining current-portion-of-LT-debt with pure short-term borrowings; lease liabilities (current 38,625) excluded as a separate line. long_term_borrowings = 'Interest bearing borrowings' non-current only (777,826); non-current lease liability (348,685) excluded. cash_and_equivalents (397,743) is the gross balance-sheet 'Cash & cash equivalents' line, NOT netted against the 7,740,597 of short-term borrowings the way the cash-flow statement's own 'analysis of cash & cash equivalents' note nets them (that note shows a net negative cash position of (7,342,854), which is a liquidity-management presentation choice, not the balance-sheet cash figure). capex (126,323) = 'Acquisition of property, plant and equipment/intangible asset'. Shares in issue (598,605,680) per Note 04 Stated Capital; EPS 0.25 = 149,938/598,605,680 matches printed 'Diluted and Basic Earnings Per Share' exactly (no separate diluted figure disclosed -- basic=diluted). trade_receivables (4,808,659) is 'Trade and other receivables' only; 'Advances and prepayments' (832,847) is a separate BS line and excluded, per this project's convention of not folding prepayments into trade_receivables. total_assets(18,839,101) = total_liabilities(13,459,261) + total_equity(5,379,840), exact. Aluminium/FX: this interim report contains ONLY the financial statements and notes -- no MD&A/directors' commentary section -- so there is no explicit management text on aluminium billet input costs or FX exposure; the input-cost and FX story is inferred from the numbers themselves (see key_drivers/gaps_note).

interim_updates.note_text: Alumex PLC (ALUM) reported revenue of Rs.3,575.6mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), down 3.8% YoY from Rs.3,717.8mn, but gross profit rose 19.0% YoY to Rs.733.9mn (from Rs.616.5mn) because cost of sales fell faster than revenue -- down 8.4% YoY to Rs.2,841.7mn (from Rs.3,101.2mn) -- lifting gross margin from 16.6% to 20.5%, consistent with aluminium billet input costs easing more than selling prices did. Results from operating activities rose 23.5% YoY to Rs.270.2mn (from Rs.218.9mn) even after distribution expenses rose 10.9% to Rs.162.2mn and administrative expenses rose 20.2% to Rs.311.1mn. Below the operating line, finance income surged from Rs.65.5mn to Rs.185.9mn (>100% YoY) while finance costs also rose 27.8% to Rs.324.4mn (from Rs.253.8mn) -- net finance costs nonetheless improved 26.5% to Rs.(138.5)mn. Profit before tax swung to Rs.131.8mn from just Rs.30.5mn (>100% YoY), and a tax reversal of Rs.18.2mn this quarter (versus a Rs.9.1mn expense a year earlier) pushed profit after tax up more than sevenfold to Rs.149.9mn (from Rs.21.4mn), with basic EPS rising to Rs.0.25 from Rs.0.04. The balance sheet shows a large working-capital swing behind this: inventories rose 38.7% since the 31 March 2026 year-end, from Rs.4,428.1mn to Rs.6,143.6mn (a Rs.1,715.5mn build per the cash flow statement), which is the single largest driver of net cash used in operating activities widening to Rs.(1,354.7)mn from Rs.(589.3)mn a year earlier -- consistent with Alumex, an aluminium extruder, building imported aluminium billet stock. Short-term interest-bearing borrowings rose to Rs.7,740.6mn (from Rs.6,470.9mn at 31 March 2026), which plausibly funded part of that inventory build and is also the likely source of the higher gross finance costs.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for ALUM in this database, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column (quarter ended 30 June 2025) is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) this interim report contains only the financial statements, notes and investor-information pages -- there is no MD&A / directors' commentary section, so no explicit management text on aluminium billet cost trends or FX exposure exists in this filing; the input-cost and FX drivers cited above are inferred from the financial-statement line items themselves, not from company commentary. (2) Finance income (Rs.185.9mn) and finance costs (Rs.324.4mn) are each disclosed as single gross lines with no note breaking either into interest vs foreign-exchange components, so the FX-gain/loss content of the >100% jump in finance income could not be isolated and is not claimed as a specific driver. (3) depreciation_amortization (Rs.130.1mn) is a single combined cash-flow addback with no PPE-vs-intangible-vs-ROU split disclosed.
interim_updates.takeaway: PAT rose >100% YoY (Rs.21.4mn to Rs.149.9mn) mainly on gross-margin expansion (16.6% to 20.5%, as cost of sales fell 8.4% against a smaller 3.8% revenue decline -- an aluminium billet input-cost tailwind) plus a Rs.18.2mn tax reversal versus a Rs.9.1mn expense a year earlier. The quarter also saw a sharp inventory build (+Rs.1,715.5mn since 31 March 2026, to Rs.6,143.6mn) funded partly by higher short-term borrowings (Rs.7,740.6mn from Rs.6,470.9mn), which pushed net operating cash flow more negative (Rs.(1,354.7)mn from Rs.(589.3)mn) and drove gross finance costs up 27.8% to Rs.324.4mn -- even though net finance costs improved on a >100% jump in finance income.
operational_highlights: Revenue fell 3.8% YoY to Rs.3,575.6mn (from Rs.3,717.8mn), but gross profit rose 19.0% to Rs.733.9mn as cost of sales fell 8.4% to Rs.2,841.7mn -- gross margin expanded from 16.6% to 20.5%
Results from operating activities up 23.5% YoY to Rs.270.2mn (from Rs.218.9mn) despite distribution expenses +10.9% (Rs.162.2mn) and administrative expenses +20.2% (Rs.311.1mn)
Finance income surged to Rs.185.9mn from Rs.65.5mn (>100% YoY); finance costs also rose 27.8% to Rs.324.4mn (from Rs.253.8mn) -- net finance costs still improved 26.5% to Rs.(138.5)mn

Profit before tax swung to Rs.131.8mn from Rs.30.5mn (>100% YoY); a Rs.18.2mn tax reversal (vs a Rs.9.1mn expense a year earlier) lifted profit after tax to Rs.149.9mn from Rs.21.4mn; basic EPS Rs.0.25 from Rs.0.04

Inventories rose 38.7% since 31 March 2026 (Rs.4,428.1mn to Rs.6,143.6mn), a Rs.1,715.5mn build per the cash flow statement -- consistent with aluminium billet stock accumulation -- and the dominant reason net cash used in operating activities widened to Rs.(1,354.7)mn from Rs.(589.3)mn a year earlier
Short-term interest-bearing borrowings rose to Rs.7,740.6mn (from Rs.6,470.9mn at 31 March 2026), plausibly funding the inventory build and contributing to the higher gross finance costs
key_drivers: Gross margin expansion from 16.6% to 20.5% (cost of sales -8.4% YoY vs revenue -3.8%) -- the primary driver of operating-profit growth, consistent with easing aluminium billet input costs relative to selling prices for this aluminium extrusion business
Tax Reversal of Rs.18.2mn this quarter vs a Rs.9.1mn tax expense a year earlier -- a Rs.27.3mn positive swing that is the single largest driver of PAT growth outrunning PBT growth

Finance income more than tripled to Rs.185.9mn (from Rs.65.5mn) -- the filing does not break this line down further (no separate interest-income vs FX-gain note), so the exact split between interest income and any FX gain on the Company's USD-denominated aluminium payables could not be determined (see gaps_note)

Rs.1,715.5mn inventory build since the 31 March 2026 year-end, funded partly by a Rs.1,269.7mn rise in short-term borrowings (Rs.6,470.9mn to Rs.7,740.6mn) -- widened net operating cash outflow to Rs.(1,354.7)mn and is the likely driver of the 27.8% rise in gross finance costs to Rs.324.4mn
